title: NASim tiny bruteforce evaluation task
description: Published evaluation-protocol contract for the admitted public NASim case (tiny static benchmark, run_bruteforce_agent baseline). Carries the reward, evaluator, and metric intent that RAES SDL deliberately excludes. Native reward scalars, the flat action index, and the raw observation vector remain source-private; only bounded measure definitions are portable.

evaluation_protocol.intent: Measure attacker progress, reward, goal attainment, and terminal cause for the admitted public protocol without asserting deterministic replay or outcome equivalence.

steps_to_termination.name: Steps to termination
steps_to_termination.measured_construct: Attacker steps to source-native goal, or the step limit when truncation occurs first.

cumulative_attacker_reward.name: Cumulative attacker reward
cumulative_attacker_reward.measured_construct: Per-episode cumulative attacker reward, where each step reward is the source-native action value minus action cost; these are the evaluator scalars, not an SDL objective score or equivalence claim.

goal_reached.name: Goal reached
goal_reached.measured_construct: Whether every sensitive host was compromised before the step limit.

terminal_cause.name: Terminal cause
terminal_cause.measured_construct: Reconstructed terminal cause, one of goal or step-limit; the terminated (goal) and truncated (step limit) causes stay distinct.

intended_use: Define the portable evaluation protocol for the admitted public NASim case so an attested run can be scored consistently.
non_use: Do not treat this synthetic example as an outcome-equivalence benchmark.
population_or_construct: A single bruteforce baseline attacker on the fixed NASim tiny three-host topology with no defender.

split_and_leakage_controls.partitioning_strategy: Single held-out public protocol run of the documented bruteforce baseline against the static tiny benchmark.

notes: Requires the separately installed qualified NASim source and the nasim-tiny backend; the supplied agents require gymnasium 0.26.x and importing NASim requires Tk system libraries.

validity_notes.note: Action success is drawn from the global NumPy RNG, not the gym reset seed, and the static benchmark ignores its constructor seed, so no run under this protocol is a deterministic replay unless the global NumPy seed is bound explicitly.
The packaged topology is intentionally small and supports workflow validation, not broad empirical claims.
